headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: Aider’s writable shared git repo can feed Perplexity’s browsing context, while Perplexity’s vendor-hosted outputs may be treated as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write the shared git repo and modify git state, while Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Aider’s repo content is copied into Perplexity or vice versa. The pathway is not fully automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Aider-generated repo content is pasted or uploaded into Perplexity as source material, THEN prompt-injection risk is present.
IF Perplexity output is copied back into Aider without review, THEN malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Keep Perplexity inputs limited to sanitized excerpts, not raw repo files.
Add a manual review step before copying Perplexity text into Aider.
Use a separate scratch branch for any files sent to Perplexity.
Strip instructions/comments from files before upload.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to repo excerpts and search outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history in a shared repo, and Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context on vendor infrastructure. If code or history is uploaded to Perplexity, sensitive repository data can leave the local environment. The pair does not prove automatic leakage, but the default vendor-hosted processing makes the pathway real.
conditions: IF source code or git history from Aider is uploaded into Perplexity, THEN repository data is exposed to vendor-hosted processing.
IF Perplexity retains browsing context for the session, THEN copied secrets may persist in its context window.
mitigations: Avoid uploading secrets or private diffs to Perplexity.
Redact credentials from files before analysis.
Use minimal excerpts instead of whole repositories.
Clear Perplexity sessions after sensitive queries.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has filesystem write and git-state modification, while Perplexity can run browser-based analysis and store session context. They do not share direct write surfaces, but they can both act on the same project artifacts through the shared repo and copied outputs. That overlap can cause conflicting edits or stale state, though not the high-severity same-dir unrestricted write case.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository artifacts in parallel, THEN conflicting changes can occur.
IF Perplexity-derived recommendations are applied to files already modified by Aider, THEN stale-state conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Use one agent at a time on a given branch.
Pull and rebase before applying any edits from Aider.
Keep Perplexity in read-only research mode for the repo.
Review diffs before committing.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared project artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers and browsing summaries that Aider may treat as actionable guidance when editing code. Aider can then commit changes directly to git, so an error in Perplexity can cascade into irreversible repository changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, making the default workflow dangerous.
conditions: IF Aider applies Perplexity output as authoritative without independent verification, THEN incorrect code changes can be committed.
IF Perplexity cites a wrong source and Aider follows it, THEN the error propagates into git history.
mitigations: Require human review of Perplexity outputs before editing.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Use Aider’s revert workflow immediately after suspicious commits.
Limit Perplexity to research, not instructions for code changes.
requires-engineering: add automated verification of cited claims before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles model-provider API keys and source code locally, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context. If regulated or confidential code is uploaded to Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may differ from local handling. The profiles do not show a specific regulated-data class, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF confidential code or regulated documents are uploaded from Aider into Perplexity, THEN vendor retention/residency terms apply to that data.
IF the organization requires local-only handling for source code, THEN Perplexity use creates a compliance mismatch.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity.
Check retention settings before use.
Use anonymized excerpts for research.
Keep secrets out of repo files.
requires-engineering: formalize a data-handling policy for cross-tool workflows.
